purpose: Evaluate scenario/query-level representational adequacy for pharmaceutical resilience and critical-medicine vulnerability without treating controlled scenarios as predictive or operational validation.
freeze_rule: Scenario definitions, assumptions, expected query outcomes, representability categories, provenance expectations and missing-evidence sensitivity rules are frozen before evaluator execution.
claim_boundary: The scenarios are controlled evaluation cases. PASS may support representational/scenario adequacy only. It does not establish prediction accuracy, causal validity, intervention effectiveness, stockout prevention, recovery performance, operational resilience, or real-world supply-chain completeness.

scenarios.title: Critical medicine single-provider disruption
scenarios.question: Can the model represent a critical medicinal product that depends on one provider affected by a disruption and is associated with a shortage in a jurisdiction?

scenarios.title: Alternative medicine under provider disruption
scenarios.question: Can the model represent an explicit alternative medicinal product for a disrupted product while preserving the disrupted dependency?

scenarios.title: Jurisdictional shortage versus physical geography
scenarios.question: Can shortage jurisdiction remain semantically distinct from the physical geography of a facility implicated in the scenario?

scenarios.title: Risk treatment and recovery boundary
scenarios.question: Can a treatment activity address an identified vulnerability, and can completed recovery be represented explicitly?
scenarios.expected_gap: No explicit RecoveryEvent/RecoveredState concept and no explicit RiskTreatmentPlan-to-RiskTreatmentActivity relation are present in the frozen ontology. Vulnerability also lacks an explicit bearer property, retained from E3 as a known extension warning.

scenarios.title: Sensitivity to missing supply evidence
scenarios.question: Does removing the provider edge from an otherwise exposed critical-medicine scenario change the executable exposure query from supported to evidence-insufficient rather than being interpreted as resilience?

conditions: All required ontology terms referenced by the frozen scenarios resolve or are recorded as an expected gap.
All frozen executable scenario queries return their expected outcomes.
Each scenario has explicit controlled provenance records.
The missing-evidence sensitivity test changes outcome exactly as frozen and is interpreted as evidence insufficiency rather than negative domain truth.
No first-pass ontology change is made to improve scenario results.
All partial/gap findings remain visible in the report.
